title: sysfs text attributes as a stable machine-consumed ABI
summary: Source-backed research candidate for a recurring semantic dependency. No active KOLVRT consumer, compatibility implementation or measured cost is claimed.

history.linux_behavior: sysfs exposes attributes as text and treats attribute names and directory structure as a documented kernel/userspace ABI.
history.historical_reason: Simple attributes expose kernel object information to userspace with a documented interface.
history.root_cause: Consumers can depend on text syntax, path topology and attribute lifecycle, beyond the underlying device operation.
history.unknown_origin_reason: The pinned documentation establishes the described behavior, not its first introducing release/commit. Historical origin requires separate investigation.

sources.title: Linux v6.12: filesystems/sysfs.rst
sources.limitations: Pinned documentation reviewed; original introduction/publication date, representative driver users and historical causality remain unverified.

native.behavior: Native boundaries use explicit typed/versioned contracts. A native device-status service and a sysfs personality have not been admitted or implemented.
native.why_differs: If actual consumers need the Linux text ABI, conversion belongs in an EL0 compatibility service rather than defining native device semantics.

security_impact: Text access must mediate only caller-authorized device effects; readable attributes are not ambient authority.
complexity_impact: Requires per-attribute version/lifecycle evidence, not a universal filesystem facade or synthetic support count.

support.owner_unknown_reason: No supported implementation/consumer owner has been assigned.
support.migration_target: Replace text/path-dependent consumption with the admitted native typed status contract; no replacement is implemented yet.
support.migration_strategy: Identify named consumers and the accepted native contract before proposing compatibility; native rewrite or deferral remain options.
support.removal_condition: No implementation currently exists. Any future implementation needs finite support, named consumers including offline/archival paths and proven quiescence; retain this historical record even if the candidate is rejected.

lifecycle.decision: Assign stable research identity after reviewing pinned semantic evidence; support/incompatibility confirmation remains open.
